title: MORSE-Face Dataset:  A Multi-Distance, Occlusion-Rich, Real and Spoof Evaluation Face Dataset
content: Face presentation attacks remain a challenge for face recognition under long stand-off distances, cross-device capture, and partial occlusion. We introduce the MORSE-Face dataset for controlled evaluation under these factors. Collected between January 2025 and February 2026, it includes 250 participants across 283 sessions in indoor and outdoor environments, captured using a DSLR and a smartphone at distances from 1m to 100m. The dataset contains over 15,700 images and 15,700 videos (approximately 1.3TB) with demographic annotations (age, gender, race). It includes live samples, structured occlusions (hair changes, facial obstructions, eyewear), and presentation attacks using 2D artifacts (printed photos, cloth masks) and 3D masks (3D printed and silicone), with conditions recorded both with and without additional props under matched distance and environment. Baseline Rank-1 recognition experiments show near-saturated performance at short range (1--10m) under same-device conditions, with degradation at longer distances and under cross-device scenarios. Indoor and outdoor results show distance-dependent trends, with performance also influenced by environmental conditions, while occlusion introduces distance-dependent degradation across prop categories. A baseline PAD experiment using a ResNet-50 classifier on live, props, and spoof samples shows high separability with minor confusion between live and prop categories. MORSE-Face highlights the gap between short-range evaluation and real-world deployment and supports research in distance-aware recognition, cross-device matching, occlusion sensitivity, and PAD with demographic analysis.
